## Priority decision

Two conditions required a rendered change today:

1. the website still described `v1.0.6` while the product repository had released `v1.0.15` on 12 August 2026;
2. the last qualifying substantive publication was the Cursor integration on 10 August 2026, so waiting until the next daily cycle would breach the rolling 48-hour content target.

The current `/architecture/` canonical already owned the distributed-runtime reader decision, so the cycle refreshed that page rather than creating a duplicate Blog or release URL. The old architecture copy also described Site Gateway/federation as if it were part of the released boundary; current product source supports Local, Direct, Controller-managed access, organizations, roles, and capabilities instead.

## Product research

Primary product sources were pinned to AgentSight `v1.0.15`:

- GitHub release `v1.0.15`, published `2026-08-12T12:19:39Z`;
- Controller architecture and authorization documentation at release commit `ba140444...`;
- Node capability implementation at the same release commit;
- Direct pairing/connection implementation at the same release commit;
- product PR `#166`, which made Direct Node access independent of Controller Relay;
- product PR `#170`, which introduced organization-scoped Nodes, built-in roles, plan semantics, and capability authorization.

Current released boundaries used by the website:

- detailed runtime data remains authoritative on AgentSight Nodes;
- Controller stores identity, organizations/memberships, organization config, plan/entitlement metadata, Node discovery, relay credentials/presence, and relay authorization decisions;
- Controller does not persist snapshots, session transcripts, prompts, process data, or relay response bodies;
- Direct remains a usable transport without Controller Relay when the browser can reach a paired Node;
- Direct pairing exchanges bootstrap authority for a scoped Node capability;
- Node-local capability actions are `node.info`, `evidence.read`, `session.read`, and `session.message`, with optional session restriction;
- built-in organization roles are viewer, operator, admin, and owner;
- canonical plans are Free, Pro, Team, and Enterprise, with Contributor Lifetime Pro applying to a contributor's personal organization.
